classification.difficultyReason: The auxiliary-angle method is explicitly required; match coefficients and signs, then select all solutions in each shifted interval.

content.prompt: Solve the following equations in the domain $0\le x\le2\pi$ by first converting to auxiliary angle form.

answer.worked:
Write the left-hand side as $R\sin(x-\alpha)$.

$$\begin{align*}R\cos\alpha&=1\\R\sin\alpha&=\sqrt3\\R&=\sqrt{1+3}=2\\\alpha&=\frac\pi3.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sin x-\sqrt3\cos x&=2\sin\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)\\2\sin\left(x-\frac\pi3\right)&=0\\x-\frac\pi3&=0,\pi\\x&=\frac\pi3,\frac{4\pi}3.\end{align*}$$

Write the left-hand side as $R\sin(x+\alpha)$.

$$\begin{align*}R\sin\alpha&=\sqrt3\\R\cos\alpha&=3\\R&=\sqrt{3+9}=2\sqrt3\\\alpha&=\frac\pi6.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sqrt3\cos x+3\sin x&=2\sqrt3\sin\left(x+\frac\pi6\right)\\2\sqrt3\sin\left(x+\frac\pi6\right)&=3\\\sin\left(x+\frac\pi6\right)&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\\x+\frac\pi6&=\frac\pi3,\frac{2\pi}3\\x&=\frac\pi6,\frac\pi2.\end{align*}$$

These are all solutions for $0\le x\le2\pi$.
